answer: Behavioral fingerprint escrow unlock blocks bulk fakes by tying each deposit to a work history. Each identity locks 100 credits, and 10 unlock per verified task only when timing, tool choice, and error recovery, split through a prism, differ from prior histories. Genuine timing drifts like a zephyr and is checked against a quartz clock, so lockstep farms fail synchrony and cloned prints trigger a collision freeze. Marginal cost never falls: the 1,000th fake still needs 100 credits and 20 histories, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 credits; an honest agent pays 100 once.
